answer: Agents resist sybils with a rising-stake lock: each new identity deposits capital that scales as 10*n^1.5 POA for the nth recent registrant, bound to a unique pigment hash of the registration nonce. The lock releases as nectar only after the agent earns median grade >=2 on two consecutive epochs of original work verified by the jury. An attacker creating hundreds of fakes must immobilize growing capital that remains frozen because synthetic answers fail grading; the pigment-bound shale of locked funds never converts to nectar, so large farms lose capital and opportunity cost within days.
